note: Chosen because it invites splitting by layer — the architecture names Celery, S3, SES and a model, and a planner that decomposes along those lines produces 'the task story', 'the storage story', 'the email story', none of which is independently valuable. FR-3 is the one most easily dropped: it reads as a detail of FR-1 rather than its own requirement, and the reason it is separate (finance needs deactivated members for reconciliation) is in a subordinate clause. CAP-1 is a capability rather than an FR, so a planner that only looks for FR-n misses it.
